A.best_element: A concrete Google-auth playbook for an extension with no backend: a personal-use GCP project setup guide, publishing to production to escape the 7-day refresh-token expiry, Desktop-client loopback for Firefox, base32hex event IDs (it notes the 'sgw' prefix is invalid), and the 409/cancelled-ID trap
A.biggest_weakness: Lopsided toward Google auth: it never mentions the ToS ban on extensions, and the DOM overlay, snipe safety, no-live-writes rule and drift canary get only a line each

B.best_element: Honest reliability tiers: T0 extension-only with alarm reconcile and catch-up, T1 Chrome background permission plus keep-awake, T2 a companion sniper. Paired with freezing contracts in Phase 0 before parallel work starts
B.biggest_weakness: Leaves the ToS as unverified even though it is findable. It never mandates a kill switch, audit log, untrusted-listing-text handling or a token-storage design, and it states the Google loopback redirect as fact without a verify flag

D.best_element: A Site Adapter split into Dom, Api, Session and Clock adapters, with versioned selectors and endpoints and a healthCheck() that disables all write automation on drift. Also a read-only Task 0 whose fixtures are the only thing downstream tasks may use
D.biggest_weakness: Says Playwright loads the unpacked extension in Firefox, which it cannot. That would leave the plan with a broken Firefox E2E lane. It also has no prior-art section and little on XSS from listing text or token-at-rest handling

E.best_element: Never hide silently: collapsed stubs, a 'N hidden · show' bar, a per-card 'Why?', and undo. Plus two insights others missed: auto-favoriting may attract rival bidders (so make it per-watch) and the shipping/landed-cost pain
E.biggest_weakness: A long UX mandate ('treat as requirements': side panel, WCAG AA, dark mode, a full UX-spec deliverable) inflates the MVP. It also states unverified items as fact ('no clock extension', 30-day account cap) and is thin on security and bid idempotency

F.best_element: A mock buyerapi with injectable latency, clock skew, error codes, token expiry and soft-close, plus total-open-exposure caps, auto-kill on anomalies, outcome classification, and real-money tests only on a user-approved cheap item
F.biggest_weakness: Spends most of its words on the nice-to-have snipe engine while overlay, daily check and calendar get a few lines. It also claims Playwright extension E2E on both browsers, though Firefox is unsupported

rationale: D gives Fable verified, site-specific recon that removes the most Phase-0 risk: card DOM, API quirks, a JWT bound to IP and user agent, the Bid-cookie 403 and the ToS quote. It also mandates an adapter layer whose healthCheck fails closed by disabling writes, which is the best single safety-plus-executability idea on the ballot. B is a close second with better platform-reliability facts and a stricter contract-freeze process. B loses because it leaves the ToS and the security controls (kill switch, audit log, untrusted input) unspecified, while D's main flaw, Playwright on Firefox, is one fixable line.
